talking_points.headline: Fed's first hike since 2023 tips Hang Seng into correction, HKMA follows to 4.25%
talking_points.context_html: Following the yen-carry unwind and rate-hike anticipation we tracked through the week of 13 September, the Federal Reserve today delivered its first hike since 2023 — 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00% — and the HKMA moved in lockstep to 4.25%. The Hang Seng Index slid into correction territory, its lowest level since July and down over 11% from this year's high. For Adam, a higher-for-longer HKD rate environment tightens margin lending and pressures leveraged wealth books precisely as WPB's Asia growth targets assume continued AUM momentum — this is the macro backdrop against which every change-execution and cost decision this quarter will be read.
source_links: Why Hang Seng Is Tumbling Today (Sep 17)

talking_points.headline: HSBC quietly ends Hong Kong school-fee perk for new hires as Elhedery's cost drive bites
talking_points.context_html: HSBC has ended the HK$300,000-a-child school-fee subsidy for new Hong Kong hires and internal transfers, retaining it only for existing band-three staff and managing directors. It's the latest cut under Georges Elhedery, HSBC Group CEO, whose overhaul has already trimmed thousands of roles and flattened management layers against a $1.5bn cost target. For Adam, this lands directly on his own change-execution mandate: a visible, symbolically loaded perk cut in the city where WPB APAC is headquartered raises retention risk for the international talent his function needs, just as JPMorgan, UBS and Schroders compete for the same senior hires.
source_links: HSBC Cuts $38K School Perk for HK Bankers

talking_points.headline: Schroders raids JPMorgan and Standard Chartered for senior Asia wealth roles
talking_points.context_html: Schroders Wealth Management has hired Andrea Li, Head of Investment Advisory Asia from JPMorgan Private Bank and Jyane Quek, Head of Marketing & Communications Asia from Standard Chartered, alongside a senior UHNW relationship manager from a Thai family office. It's a reminder that Asia's private-banking talent war extends beyond HSBC's usual competitor set — pure-play wealth managers are now bidding for the same senior advisory and family-office talent. For Adam, it sharpens the retention case at exactly the moment HSBC is trimming perks like the Hong Kong school-fee subsidy: the war for advisory talent is intensifying just as HSBC's own value proposition to that talent is being cut.
source_links: Schroders Expands Asia Team From JPM, StanChart

HSBC News.title: HSBC Cuts Back $38,000-a-Kid School Perk for Some Hong Kong Bankers
HSBC News.summary: HSBC has ended its education subsidy, which covered up to 95% of school fees (up to HK$300,000/US$38,000 per child at secondary level), for new hires and staff transferring into Hong Kong, though existing band-three employees and managing directors keep the benefit. The cut is part of CEO Georges Elhedery's cost-trimming campaign, which has already included thousands of job cuts and a flattening of management layers, and has reportedly caused friction with London staff who have no equivalent perk.

Regulatory & Markets.title: Fed's First Hike Since 2023 Tips Hang Seng Into Correction; HKMA Follows to 4.25%
Regulatory & Markets.summary: The Federal Reserve raised rates 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00% — its first hike since 2023 — and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority followed in lockstep with its own 25bp move to 4.25%. The Hang Seng Index slid into correction territory, touching its lowest level since July and down more than 11% from this year's high, with technology and financial names, including several HSBC-linked peers, leading the losses.

Competitor Intelligence.title: Schroders Wealth Management Expands Asia Team With Hires From JPMorgan, Standard Chartered
Competitor Intelligence.summary: Schroders Wealth Management, which manages roughly $196 billion globally, has added three senior hires to its Asia team: Andrea Li as Head of Investment Advisory Asia (from JPMorgan Private Bank), a senior UHNW/family-office relationship manager from a Thai family office, and Jyane Quek as Head of Marketing & Communications Asia (from Standard Chartered).

Private Banking & Wealth.title: Global Ultra-Wealthy Ranks Increase at Double-Digit Pace, Altrata Finds
Private Banking & Wealth.summary: Altrata's World Ultra Wealth Report 2026 finds the global UHNW population (net worth over $30 million) reached an all-time high of 556,850 individuals in 2025 — a second consecutive year of double-digit growth, the strongest since 2017. The US added the most UHNW individuals in absolute terms, but Asia-Pacific posted the fastest regional growth and now holds roughly 31% of the global UHNW population.
